text: Coding theory: random linear codes meeting a fixed set , the first-moment count behind the list-decodability of random linear codes (Guruswami, Håstad and Kopparty, IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory 57, 2011). Translation: a block's clause \(g_{b,i}[C_bg=0]\) forbids exactly the points whose zero pattern \(z\in\{0,1\}^h\) is nonzero and lies in \(\ker C_b\), a random subspace of codimension at most \(t\). Coding theory's first moment says a random subspace meets a fixed set \(Z\) in about \(|Z|3^{-t}\) points. What it would give: for any fixed probability distribution \(\mu\) on assignments, for example a pseudo-distribution built from a weak PHP design, the family's forbidden set has small \(\mu\)-measure. Smallest test: the expectation. For a fixed point with zero pattern \(z\ne0\), \(\Pr_C[Cz=0]=3^{-t}\), since \(C\) is uniform. So \(\mathbb E_C[\mu(\text{forbidden by }b)]\le3^{-t}\), and over \(M\le n^K\) blocks, \(\mathbb E[\mu(\text{forbidden})]\le M3^{-t}\le1/(3n)\) at \(t=\lceil(K+1)\log_3n\rceil+1\). By Markov, with probability at least \(1-n^{-1/2}/3\) the forbidden set has \(\mu\)-measure below \(n^{-1/2}\). This holds for every family, dense or not, and for every \(\mu\) that does not depend on the \(C_b\). A dual object built for the specific randomized system, such as a pseudo-expectation against a given refutation attempt, is therefore not covered; only objects determined by the family and the base are. Test. Passed.

trail.text: Coding theory: random linear codes meeting a fixed set. The small-measure entry tested it as a robustness statement: forbidden measure does not control PC degree, under both natural distributions. Follow-up. Closed: the measure form fails, and a structured form reduces to the recorded vacuity question.

text: Bollobás's configuration model and Friedman's theorem on random regular graphs , for the biregular residual. Target: the re-proof of the residual lemmas. A random biregular graph is a uniformly random pairing of degree slots, and expansion of small sets follows by the same union bound with slot counts. Where it breaks: the residual-column lemma needs, for a block, the probability that given pigeons have neighbours in given holes, and pairings are only negatively correlated, not independent. Test. Passed for left expansion only. In the pairing model, the probability that \(u\) pigeons' \(5u\) slots all land among \(3u\) given holes, each of degree at most 6, is at most \(\binom{18u}{5u}/\binom{5\cdot(h+1)}{5u}\le(18u/(5h))^{5u}\). That is of the same order as the independent bound \((3u/h)^{5u}\), so the union bound goes through with a larger constant. The simple biregular graph is the pairing conditioned on being simple, an event of probability bounded below by a constant at bounded degrees, which costs a constant factor. Hole-side expansion and the column lemma were not checked.

trail.text: Bollobás's configuration model, for a biregular residual. The chain residual kept independent 5-subsets for the ordinary residual pigeons and handled the hole side with the chain, so no biregular model was needed. Follow-up. Closed: not needed.

text: Low-density parity-check codes over \(\mathbb F_3\). Translation: the edges of the residual graph are code symbols, and rows and onto columns are ternary parity checks at the vertices. Q's \(\mathbb F_3\)-solutions of the linear part form a coset of this code. Q has no Boolean collision-free solutions at all. What a theorem there would give: rigidity of the solution coset, which low-degree pseudo-solutions might violate. Smallest test: whether the code is nontrivial, and its distance. Test. Passed for nontriviality only. The code has \(|E|=5m\) symbols and \(m+N\) checks with one dependency, so its dimension is at least \(4m-N+1>0\), with equality when the graph is connected. It is the cycle code of the graph: an alternating \(\pm1\) cycle is a codeword, so its minimum distance is the girth, \(O(\log N)\), not linear. Sipser and Spielman's linear distance needs symbols on vertices or good constituent codes. So the bridge gives no rigidity in this form.

trail.text: Low-density parity-check codes over \(\mathbb F_3\). Since that review, no entry used the code, and the chain residual made the rigidity question moot. Follow-up. Closed: it is a cycle code, each cell lying in exactly one row check and one column check, so its distance is the girth, at most \(O(\log N)\) by the Moore bound and constant with constant probability for the random residual. It gives no rigidity, and the route no longer needs it.

text: Multicomponent lattice gases in chemistry: conservation of each species. Translation: pigeons of different weight classes are different chemical species, and holes are lattice sites holding at most one particle. A weighted column sum \(C^\alpha_t\) is the species at site \(t\). Pinning all of them fixes the species at every site, a separate conservation law for each species. What a theorem there would give: separability, since species that do not interact decouple. Here it would say that PHP with site species pinned is a product of one-species problems. Smallest test: the decomposition. Test. Passed. Take weight vectors \(\alpha^0,\alpha^1,\dots,\alpha^r\in\mathbb F_3^{n+1}\) with \(\alpha^0\) all ones, and let the type of pigeon \(i\) be \((\alpha^0_i,\dots,\alpha^r_i)\). No pigeon has type 0. Pin \(C^{\alpha^k}_t=\tau^{(k)}_t\) for all \(k,t\). Restrict \(x_{it}=0\) whenever the type of \(i\) differs from \(\tau_t\). Each pin on a hole with \(\tau_t=\theta\ne0\) becomes \(\theta^{(k)}\) times its onto column, or \(0=0\), and a hole with \(\tau_t=0\) is empty. The restricted system is, variable-disjointly for each type \(\theta\), an onto system of the type-\(\theta\) pigeons into the holes with \(\tau_t=\theta\). Refuting a variable-disjoint union costs at least as much as refuting any one part, by restricting the others to satisfying assignments. Allocation: pick the largest class \(\theta^*\), with \(m_{\theta^*}\ge(n+1)/3^r\ge6\) pigeons. Give it \(m_{\theta^*}-3\) holes, every other class \(\theta\) exactly \(m_\theta\) holes, satisfiable by a matching, and leave two holes empty. This uses \(n\) holes. The pins are consistent with the rows at degree 1: for each \(k\), \(\sum_t\tau^{(k)}_t=\sum_i\alpha^k_i-3\theta^{*(k)}\equiv\sum_i\alpha^k_i\), which is \(\sum_tC^{\alpha^k}_t\) modulo the rows. The pins need not be values of a Boolean assignment, since prop:occupancy-pin-reduction fixes an arbitrary pin vector. The hard class inherits the spare-pigeon bound \(\lceil(m_{\theta^*}-3)/2\rceil+1\).

trail.text: Multicomponent lattice gases. Developed into thm:type-pinning in the type-pinning entry , whose capacity this review measures: about \(\log_3n\) family-wide weight vectors, and nothing for generic families. Follow-up. Closed: developed into a theorem; its capacity is exhausted on generic dense families.

text: Dilute quenched disorder in statistical physics: the Harris criterion. Translation: each generic dense block is an impurity that forbids a random fraction \(3^{-t}\approx n^{-(K+1)}\) of the configurations, independently of the others given the forms. The whole family is a dilute quenched disorder of total density \(O(1/n)\) on the PHP ensemble. A theorem there says when weak disorder is irrelevant: it does not change the critical behaviour. Here that would be the PC degree. What it would give: a principle that dilute random constraints do not lower degree, for the right notion of dilution. Smallest test: whether the density is dilute in the relevant sense. Test. Passed as a count: the expected forbidden fraction is at most \(n^K3^{-t}\le1/(3n)\) under any fixed distribution, from the random-prefix review. The structured counterexamples to measure robustness are not dilute random sets. Whether PC degree obeys a Harris-type criterion is the question the bridge poses.

trail.text: Dilute quenched disorder, the Harris criterion. The dense-killer entry developed it into an exact Nullstellensatz span criterion over the functional base, with the count far below the fill point, but without a proof. Follow-up. Continuing: the criterion is exact, and whether dilute random clauses leave \(1\) outside the span is the open core.

Dilute quenched disorder, the Harris criterion. The random-wide-block entry found exact semi-regularity for random pins at the Nullstellensatz level: dilute random linear constraints cost only dimension until the design space is used up (conj:pin-semiregularity). The random bit family is the cleanest dilute-disorder instance of the adversarial core, with random codes in place of random forms. Follow-up. Continuing: the Harris picture is the heuristic for the random bit family, and no proof mechanism has come from it yet.

Dilute quenched disorder, the Harris criterion. This review's quiet-planting bridge is its planted form: the disorder is dilute (forbidden fraction at most \(1/n\)), so planting is free at the level of measures. Follow-up. Continuing: dilution is established as a count, and what is missing is a mechanism turning dilution into degree; this review's invisibility lead, the natural candidate, was falsified.

Dilute quenched disorder, the Harris criterion. Its two developments turned dilution into degree only in special cases: random pins (conj:pin-semiregularity, Nullstellensatz, random forms) and pattern-poor supports (prop:pattern-poor-support, Nullstellensatz, pattern-poor families). Follow-up. Closed: for adversarial dense families no mechanism converts dilution into degree, and the pattern count suggests the natural one cannot.

text: The killer-moment reduction (lem:product-top-moment-reduction, lem:low-rank-strata, lem:gauss-sum-killer-bound), for a block whose forms are also random. Target: one wide random block under random prefix. Where it breaks: the reduction is for product tops of degree 4 on the weak monomial algebra, and a clause has degree \(4t+2\) with a different product structure. Test. Passed on its hypothesis: its strata bounds need uniformly random forms, which a random block has. Whether the clause structure fits the reduction is the next step's question.

trail.text: The killer-moment reduction for a random block. Developed into lem:pin-moment-formula: a fixed design survives a random pin with probability exactly \(3^{-\operatorname{rank}M_\ell}\). The second moment needs joint-rank strata of pairs of designs, and the setting is random forms, off the critical path. Follow-up. Closed: the adversarial core has no randomness in the forms for the moment to use.

text: Coding theory: list recovery of random linear codes (Guruswami and Indyk; Rudra and Wootters). Translation: block \(b\) forbids the matchings whose pattern lies in the random code \(\ker C_b\), and the family is \(n^K\) independent random codes of codimension \(t\). List-recovery theorems bound how many codewords a small set of candidates can hit. What it would give: any set of \(N\) matchings meets the forbidden sets of few blocks, a sparsity of active blocks that gluing arguments need. Smallest test: the expected number of blocks active on a fixed set of \(N\) matchings. Test. Passed as a count: at most \(Nn^K3^{-t}\le N/n\) in expectation. Whether degree-\(d\) designs can be localized to such small sets is the open part.

trail.text: List recovery of random linear codes. Each set of \(N\) matchings meets at most \(N/n\) forbidden sets in expectation. Follow-up. Closed: degree-\(d\) designs are not localized to small sets of matchings, since each constraint's multiples touch every \(d\)-face, so a bound on active blocks per small set of points has no use in a design argument.

text: Statistical physics: quiet planting (Krzakala and Zdeborová, Phys. Rev. Lett. 102, 2009). Below the condensation threshold, a random constraint ensemble with a planted solution is contiguous to the unplanted one, so planting changes no typical property. Translation: the W_RS family is a random constraint ensemble on matchings; pinning or constraining at \(x^*\) plants a near-solution. What it would give: the planted view loses nothing, and a proof may use the planted point without paying for it. Smallest test: whether the density is far below any threshold. Test. Passed as a count. Each block forbids a fraction at most \(3^{-t}\le n^{-K-1}\) of any fixed distribution on points with \(g\ne0\), so \(n^K\) blocks forbid at most \(1/n\) in expectation. The planted and unplanted conditional laws of the prefix matrices then differ by \(O(1/n)\) in total variation, by the same first-moment count.

trail.text: Quiet planting. Developed into prop:pattern-poor-support: plant the whole design and count patterns. Follow-up. Closed: exact for pattern-poor families; for dense families the pattern count against the support bound suggests the union bound fails.

text: Lauria and Nordström, "Graph colouring is hard for algorithms based on Hilbert's Nullstellensatz and Gröbner bases" (CCC 2017). They prove Nullstellensatz and PC degree lower bounds for \(k\)-colouring by substituting colouring variables with polynomials in the variables of a functional pigeonhole instance over a bounded-degree bipartite graph, gadget by gadget. Each colouring axiom becomes a low-degree consequence of the source. Target: the substitution lead in the form it has left, a source hard as a whole. Where it may break: their target constraints are local, one gadget each, while W's clauses involve most cells. Test. Passed as a structural check. Their abstract (arXiv 2306.00125) states that the source is functional PHP over bounded-degree bipartite graphs, reduced to \(k\)-colouring in constant PC degree. A single pigeonhole system is not a product with a satisfiable factor, so lem:composition-collapse does not apply. No record entry cites the paper (notebook search for "Lauria": only Galesi–Lauria on ordering principles).

trail.text: Lauria and Nordström's gadget reduction from functional PHP. The gadget-substitution entry read their Section 3 in the source. The substitution is the identity on the pigeons' choices, and it defines auxiliary vertices as local functions of them. W's target has no auxiliary variables, and per-pigeon relabelling breaks the collision axioms. Follow-up. Closed: gadget substitutions need auxiliary variables that W's clauses do not have.

text: Alekhnovich and Razborov's pseudo-reduction for non-binomial constraints (Alekhnovich and Razborov, "Lower bounds for polynomial calculus: non-binomial case", Proc. Steklov Inst. Math. 242, 2003). Their design reduces a monomial modulo the constraints inside the closure of its support. It needs each constraint to be immune (no nonzero low-degree function vanishes on its allowed set) and the constraint incidence to expand. In the form-value encoding a W_RS block is one constraint on its \(h\) form values. Target: A1. Answers. It would supply the missing design for families whose blocks are individually immune and collectively expanding, with no shared pinned span; this is exactly the high-rank case the obstacle leaves. Test. Passed at the local level. prefix_immunity.py computes the immunity of one block's allowed set in \(\mathbb F_3^h\), for \(h\le6\), \(t\in\{1,2\}\), eight uniform \(C\) and two zero-column controls per case (prefix_immunity.json). For \(t=1\) the immunity is 3 to 6. For \(t=2\) it is 4 to 9, and 6 to 9 at \(h=6\). It grows with \(h\) and mostly stays below the clause degree \(4t+2\). Controls with \(C=0\) give immunity 2, the input degree, as they must. So a block's immunity is of the order of \(t\), the right scale, but below W_RS's degree \(11\delta\) by a factor that expansion would have to supply. The expansion step is not run. In the cell encoding every block touches all cells. The span-based closure is the recorded closure sub-line ( ordered closure ), whose restart needs a new expansion notion.

trail.text: Alekhnovich and Razborov's pseudo-reduction, passed locally at the route review. Developed in the support-against-immunity entry. Follow-up. Closed: their criterion lets two constraints share fewer than \(\ell/4\le t+\tfrac12\) variables, and dense forms stay dense in every basis (lem:dense-forms-every-basis).

text: Longuet-Higgins' theorem on nonbonding orbitals of alternant hydrocarbons (J. Chem. Phys. 18, 1950), from Hückel theory. Translation: the pigeon–hole board is an alternant molecule with one excess starred atom. Nonbonding orbitals are vectors annihilated by the biadjacency matrix, found by the zero-sum rule: the coefficients around each unstarred atom sum to zero. Answers. It gives the degree-1 safety condition for the pins that the obstacle's designs would use. A pin set \(\{u=v\}\) is refuted at degree 1 exactly when a zero-sum combination of the row equations and the pins is a nonzero constant. For pinned column sums \(C_j=o_j\), a combination \(\sum_ia_i(\text{row}_i-1)+\sum_jb_j(C_j-o_j)\) is constant only if \(a_i+b_j=0\) for all \(i,j\). Then it equals \(a\bigl(\sum_jo_j-(n+1)\bigr)\), which is nonzero exactly when \(\sum_jo_j\not\equiv n+1\pmod 3\). This agrees with the recorded total-occupancy condition of thm:global-closure-gluing. It says nothing above degree 1. Test. Passed (the two-line computation above).

trail.text: Longuet-Higgins' zero-sum rule, which gave the degree-1 pin safety condition. No work in these cycles: the obstacle moved from pins to connected families of members, where pin safety is not the constraint. Follow-up. Closed: its content is the degree-1 zero-sum rule, equivalent to the recorded occupancy condition, and nothing above degree 1 was found.

text: Resolvent saturation , the mechanism of thm:resolvent-taylor-glue: add the fallen consequences of degree \(\le D\) as constraints and require Taylor generation of the saturated tops. It is recorded for W's clauses and not followed for W_RS until now. Target: A3 for W_RS. Answers. It makes the gluing fall-tolerant by construction. If saturating pairs of members suffices, gluing becomes local again, at the level of pairs. Test. Passed for trees, falsified for cycles. Run here (triple_falls.m2, triple_falls.txt): three blocks, \(h=3\), \(t=1\), in the form-value model. The test compares \(\operatorname{gr}(J_1+J_2+J_3)\) with the sum of the pair saturations \(\operatorname{gr}(J_a+J_b)\). On chains (two shared forms, path nerve) the pair saturations generate the triple's graded ideal in 4 of 4 trials, although every trial had a falling pair. On triangles (cycle nerve) the triple has further falls in 3 of 4 trials: excesses 1, 1 in degrees 5 and 6; 2, 2 in 7 and 8; 3, 6, 3 in 6 to 8.

trail.text: Resolvent saturation. Follow-up. Closed: pair saturations do not generate tree families' falls in general (conj:tree-member-saturation).

text: Čech and Leray vanishing on member covers , a lead of the generalization review for adversarial families that the record names but never followed. Leray's theorem computes the cohomology of a union from the nerve of a cover when the intersections are acyclic. Target: A1 and A3. Answers. It locates the gluing obstruction in the Čech cohomology of the member cover, so hardness would follow from vanishing of the classes carried by cycles of the nerve, not from absence of falls. Test. Passed. The same computation shows new falls only when the nerve has a cycle (chains 0 of 4, triangles 3 of 4), as the Čech picture predicts. The identification of the triangle excess with a Čech class is not yet made.

trail.text: Čech and Leray vanishing on member covers. Follow-up. Closed: its prediction that new falls appear only on cycles fails for random members, where falls track density instead.

text: Lattice gauge theory and Wilson loops (physics). Translation: members are links, shared forms are gauge variables, and a fall around a cycle of the nerve is a nontrivial holonomy. Gauge fixing along a spanning tree removes every variable except the loop variables. Answers. Saturate along a spanning tree of the member nerve, which the chain test shows is fall-complete. Then only the cycle space, of dimension \(|E|-|V|+1\), carries new constraints. The global obstacle becomes a statement about loops, the analogue of Wilson loops. Test. Passed. The chain and triangle runs are the gauge-fixing test: the tree leaves no residual falls, and the one loop leaves residual falls.

trail.text: Lattice gauge theory and Wilson loops. Follow-up. Closed: it rested on the tree-and-cycle reading, which random members refute (conj:tree-member-saturation).

text: Dobrushin's uniqueness condition (statistical mechanics). If the total influence of local interactions is below 1, the Gibbs measure is unique and analytic under the perturbation. Translation: members are interactions on a base measure of near-matchings, with influence at most their forbidden fraction. Answers. In characteristic 0 it would give a fall-tolerant design for the whole connected family by perturbation, whatever the nerve, since influence is a global sum and not a local syzygy condition. Test. Passed at the level of the condition: each block forbids at most a \(3^{-t}\) fraction of patterns, and the total \(M3^{-t}\le1/(3n)<1\). The transfer to \(\mathbb F_3\) is the parked 3-integrality step ( integral extension ), and a real design of weak PHP must be signed. Neither is addressed.

trail.text: Dobrushin's uniqueness condition. Follow-up. Closed: it is conditioning, which pays degree per block ( Dobrushin conditioning ).

text: Cohen–Lenstra universality for random matrices over finite fields (Wood's universality theorems, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 2019), recorded for product tops as conj:product-top-cohen-lenstra. Target: A1 and A3 for random families. Answers. Below the fill point, random constraint systems are direct, with no falls, with probability close to 1. That is a cost scaling with probability, since dependencies appear only with their random-matrix probability. Test. Passed at the counting level: W_RS's constraint count is a factor \(n^{-\Omega(t)}\) below the fill point (falsification attempt above), so universality, if it held for the members' saturated ideals, would give no cross-member falls below \(D\). It is not yet stated for member ideals, and single members already fall, so it must be stated relative to \(\sum_b\operatorname{gr}I_b\).

trail.text: Cohen–Lenstra universality for member ideals. Follow-up. Developed over the six entries. As stated for member ideals it was refuted below the counting fill point. It became the density principle, conj:fill-point-falls for random forms, and conj:shared-piece-falls for adversarial forms with random prefixes. This review redirects it from falls to row freeness.

Cohen–Lenstra universality for member ideals. Follow-up. Closed: it produced the density, fill-point and shared-piece statements for falls. The fall-line review then showed that falls are not what the goal's sufficient condition needs, and the sub-family corollary makes them irrelevant inside capacity. Universality below the fill point is no longer the obstacle.

text: Percolation on the dependency hypergraph (branching processes). Falls spread only through shared dependencies, so if dependency clusters are small, conditioning need only pay per cluster. Answers. It would bound the cost by the size of dependency clusters, which scales with a probability rather than the number of blocks. Test. Passed for random families: by the union bound in "Revisiting", sets of up to \(N/(2h)\) blocks have independent forms. So the pairwise dependency graph is empty with high probability, and dependencies appear only at size about \(N/h\). For adversarial families the clusters are chosen by the adversary.

trail.text: Percolation on the dependency hypergraph. Follow-up. Developed: the clusters that matter are shared pieces, not dependencies. Sunflowers, chains and span dependence never fell early without a shared piece, and shared pieces occur with probability at most \(h3^{-t}\) per member. So under random prefixes the clusters have size one with high probability. This review's cluster-expansion bridge continues it.

Percolation on the dependency hypergraph. Follow-up. Closed: its prediction became lem:shared-piece-rarity (clusters of size one under random prefixes) for falls. For row freeness, clusters within capacity are row-free by the sub-family corollary. What remains is the gluing of clusters, which the Kotecký–Preiss and Mayer–Vietoris items carry.

text: Lefschetz properties of Artinian algebras (Harima, Migliore, Nagel and Watanabe, J. Algebra 262, 2003). For one row sum, row freeness of \(M\) through \(D\) says that \(r\) acts with all Jordan blocks of length 3 in low degrees, a Lefschetz-type condition. Target: A3 and W through global closure gluing. Answers. Lefschetz theory proves such conditions for quotients by general or monomial ideals, and a condition holding in low degrees is untouched by new generators of higher degree. Row freeness of \(Q\) would follow from the base's, if removing \(Q\)'s error set acts like a quotient by an ideal whose new generators start near the fill point. Test. Passed on the 2 × 8 base: all five families have the base's Jordan-type condition (\(\operatorname{Tor}_1=0\)) through degree 3, and lose it only one degree before their own fill.

trail.text: Lefschetz properties. Follow-up. Developed: the pullback lemma is the freeness-inheritance statement the lead suggested, for allowed sets pulled back from values with good fibers. Beyond capacity no Lefschetz-type input is available, and the lead gives nothing further there.

Lefschetz properties. This cycle checked what the lead could still give beyond capacity. The obstruction found there is a collapse of products modulo the row sums across members, not a failure of a single member's multiplication maps, which is what Lefschetz statements control. Follow-up. Closed: its content is the pullback lemma within capacity, and it gives nothing about cross-member collapse.

text: Smoothed analysis (Spielman and Teng, J. ACM 2004), from computer science: worst-case inputs under a small random perturbation behave like typical inputs. Translation: W_RS is a smoothed instance, with adversarial forms perturbed by random prefixes. Answers. A smoothed theorem for row freeness would show that the adversary's structure (shared pieces, dependencies) dissolves under the random prefixes. That is the form A1 needs: every family of forms, random prefixes only. Test. Passed at the level of falls: the 65 runs without a shared piece (53 in the shared-piece entry, 12 in the span check), most of them with adversarial forms, never fell early, and lem:shared-piece-rarity is a smoothed bound. The same test for row freeness needs three-row boards.

trail.text: Smoothed analysis. Follow-up. Continuing: for falls it became lem:shared-piece-rarity. For row freeness the analogue is open: whether random prefixes keep \(\rho\)-divisible and other \(\mathfrak m\)-divisible tops out of a member's first new degree. The Grassmannian lead above shows it must use the pattern structure.

Smoothed analysis. This cycle: row-shifted sunflowers show that the adversary's coincidences modulo the row sums are not smoothed by random prefixes, since prefixes randomize only the Boolean factor. Normal form removes the linear coincidences. What smoothing could still do is keep random Boolean factors from creating product collapses, the untested part named in the restricted-isometry bridge. Follow-up. Continuing.

Smoothed analysis. This cycle: the Schwartz–Zippel lead shows how randomness enters local independence, through the kernel patterns of the prefixes and not polynomially. The smoothing question is now whether random kernel patterns keep the members' Boolean factors in general position against the witness basis. Follow-up. Continuing.

Smoothed analysis. The \(U\)-shifted defect is in the tops themselves, whatever the random prefixes: randomness in the Boolean factors cannot separate tops that agree modulo \((U^2)\). Follow-up. Closed: prefix randomness does not smooth adversarial coincidences of the forms.

text: The Kotecký–Preiss cluster expansion (Comm. Math. Phys. 103, 1986), from statistical physics: a polymer gas with small activities has a convergent expansion over clusters of incompatible polymers. Translation: members are polymers, incompatibility is a shared form, and the activity is the probability \(h3^{-t}\) of a shared piece. Answers. Row-freeness defects of \(Q\) would be sums of contributions of small clusters, and the expansion would converge, with only local, rare clusters contributing. Test. Passed as arithmetic: the criterion \(\sum_{b'\sim b}w(b')e^{a}\le a\), with \(a=1\) and at most \(M\) neighbours, needs \(Mh3^{-t}\le1/e\), and W_RS has \(Mh3^{-t}\le h/(3n)\). Whether row-freeness defects are additive over clusters is untested.

trail.text: Kotecký–Preiss cluster expansion. Follow-up. Continuing: the sub-family corollary makes every cluster within capacity row-free, which is the polymer-level input. The expansion's additivity over clusters is the Mayer–Vietoris lead above, not yet tested.

Kotecký–Preiss cluster expansion. This cycle tested whether pointwise interactions between members control the defect. Row-shifted and exact sunflowers of dense flats interact pointwise in the same way, yet their defects are 778 and 49 at \(M=1000\) on 3 × 9. Follow-up. Closed: no expansion in pointwise polymer interactions can bound the purity defect, which is invisible to point statistics.

text: Dade's lemma (E. C. Dade, Ann. of Math. 108, 1978), with Carlson's rank varieties: over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\), a module over \(\Lambda\cong\overline{\mathbb F}_3[(\mathbb Z/3)^{m-1}]\) is free iff it is free over \(k[u_\alpha]/(u_\alpha^3)\) for every \(u_\alpha=\sum_i\alpha_ir_i\ne0\). Target: the obstacle. Answers. Purity against all row sums would reduce to single row forms \(u_\alpha\). Modulo one \(u_\alpha\), only shifts inside its span collapse, and lem:column-tensor-exactness gives single-form annihilators, so the adversary's collapse would have to show in one direction. Where it breaks: the record refutes a truncated version for general column tensors in special position (ex:truncated-dade-special-position), and the board's own row sums need their own statement. Test. Passed in the smallest case: on the 3 × 5 base, \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^\Lambda=0,0,0,103\) in degrees 1 to 4. All 14 distinct single directions tried (the 10 points of \(\mathbb P^1(\mathbb F_9)\) and four random directions over \(\mathbb F_{81}\); one point was run twice) give \(0,0,0,43\). So each detects the first non-free degree exactly and none fails earlier (single_direction.m2, base_3x5.txt). The 3 × 6 run exceeded the 600 s limit in Macaulay2 (base_3x6_3x7_timeout.txt).

trail.text: Dade's lemma. This cycle: the local-witness framework made single directions unnecessary on the base side, since spanning is proved directly. Its remaining use is on the adversarial side. For one direction \(u_\alpha=\sum_i\alpha_ir_i\), a change of row basis makes \(u_\alpha\) a single row sum, so the one-row theorem's witnesses describe the dual of \(\tilde A/u_\alpha\tilde A\). Local independence could then be checked one direction at a time, if a truncated Dade statement holds for the board's own row sums. Its smallest test, the 3 × 5 base, passed in the directness review. Follow-up. Continuing.

Dade's lemma. Developed in the single-direction sectors entry, which gives point-set criteria per direction and shows that full sectors are useless below \(D\). This review aims it at locating the \(U\)-shifted defect. Follow-up. Continuing.

Dade's lemma, per single row-sum direction. Developed: prop:spread-family-level-gap applies the single-direction criterion to prove a family-level failure with no condition on falls. Follow-up. Developed.
Dade's lemma. Continued this cycle as the rank-variety lead: the obstructions found are single-direction, which is exactly what rank varieties measure. Follow-up. Continuing.
Dade's lemma. Follow-up. Closed: its last form, the rank-variety weakening, fails because the single-direction obstructions carry genuine falls (prop:varying-shift-affine-fall).

text: Gauge fixing (lattice gauge theory; the Faddeev–Popov procedure). Translation: a form defined up to the row sums is a gauge orbit, because on PHP's points, where every row sum is 1, \(\ell+\rho\) and \(\ell\) differ by a constant. The row-sum ideal is the gauge ideal, and a purity defect is an observable that is gauge-trivial but nonzero before fixing. Theorem there: fix a gauge slice transversal to the orbits, and gauge-equivalent configurations become identical. Answers. Fixing the gauge by normal form makes coincidences modulo the row sums exact, and exact coincidences are what the covering mechanism absorbs. Test. Passed: part 4 of lem:row-shift-collapse. Normal form is a gauge slice, it sends every row-shifted sunflower to an exact one, and it costs nothing in the composition. This review's restatement comes from it.

trail.text: Gauge fixing. Its content, normal form as a gauge slice, is built into conj:normalized-dense-row-freeness. In the witness framework the ghost row of lem:ghost-slater-pairing makes every witness shift-invariant, so gauge invariance is automatic on the witness side. Follow-up. Closed: fully used, and the witness formalism makes it automatic.

text: Standard monomial theory through Robinson–Schensted (Shareshian–Wachs, Theorem 6.3, as cor:rsk-monomial-basis). Target: local independence as a normal-form computation. Answers. Reduction to the monomials \(\gamma(S,T)\) is a normal form for \(A\). Independence of tops then means independence of their normal forms, a leading-term question in which density could supply distinct leading monomials. Test. Passed: cor:rsk-monomial-basis is proved above, and its count matches \(\dim A_d\). Whether leading terms of adversarial tops are distinct is the development question.

trail.text: The RSK monomial basis. Not developed since. Its intended use, leading terms for independence, is overtaken by the finding that independence fails for \(U\)-shifted sunflowers. It remains the tool for normal forms modulo the row sums on distinct-row contents. Follow-up. Continuing.

The RSK monomial basis. Its intended use, leading terms for independence in normal form, is moot once the condition quantifies over equivalent families. No recorded step needs it. Follow-up. Closed: normal form is no longer the object.

text: Slater determinants and the Slater–Condon rules (quantum chemistry). Translation: rows are particles, columns are orbitals, and column-injectivity is Pauli exclusion. A simplex functional \(\rho_{A,B}\) is a Slater determinant of \(|A|\) particles in \(|A|+1\) orbitals with one hole, carried by a ghost particle. A top is a product state of the forms. Answers. The Slater–Condon rules compute overlaps of determinants with product states as sums of minors. Local independence then becomes nondegeneracy of a Gram-type matrix of bordered minors, where density means many nonvanishing minors. Test. Passed: lem:ghost-slater-pairing is that overlap formula, proved above and checked against the difference (\(k=1\)) and the triangle-area form (\(k=2\)).

trail.text: Slater determinants. Its ghost-row pairing is the witness formula that detects the defect: witnesses are shift-invariant only for full row sums, not for \(U\)-shifts. Follow-up. Continuing.
Slater determinants. Not developed this cycle. Its ghost-row witnesses remain the formula for tops-only defects, as used in prop:column-spread-defect's degree-2 functionals. Follow-up. Continuing.

Slater determinants. Checked this cycle against the new classes. Its ghost-row witnesses are product functionals on disjoint column blocks, which vanish on the row-sum ideal \(R\). So they measure rank modulo \(R\), not the defect. Every class found since the equivalence review, \(r_i\tau\) included, lies in \(R\), where these witnesses are blind. Follow-up. Closed: the witnesses vanish exactly where the remaining obstructions live.

text: Dade's lemma, per single row-sum direction (continuing lead). Target: locating the defect. Answers. Along a direction \(u\) not proportional to the occupancy, prop:single-direction-sectors turns freeness into equal Hilbert functions of the three level sets. For the \(U\)-shifted sunflower, the level sets of \(u=\sum p_ir_i\) interact with the members' column-1 perturbations, and the defect should appear as unequal level-set Hilbert functions in a specific direction. Whether one rational direction already detects the defect is open. Test. Passed: lem:u-shift-collapse shows that the images modulo \(R\) collapse along \(U\), the column-1 directions, which is where single-direction detection must look.

trail.text: Dade's lemma, aimed at locating the \(U\)-shifted defect. Developed: in the column representation the defect disappears (lem:column-representation), and the direction that detects the spread family's defect is \(r_i\) itself. Follow-up. Developed.
Dade's lemma, aimed at locating defects. Every defect found since, including \(r_i\tau\), is located in the direction of a single row sum. Follow-up. Continuing, merged with the rank-variety lead.
Dade's lemma, aimed at locating defects. Follow-up. Closed, with the rank-variety lead.

text: Degenerate perturbation theory (quantum mechanics). Translation: the shared core \(\prod w_j^2\) is the unperturbed state, each member's shifts are a perturbation of size \(\varepsilon\sim u\), and reduction modulo \((U^2)\) keeps exactly the first-order terms. Answers. In degenerate perturbation theory, first-order corrections live in the span of the perturbation applied to the degenerate state. States that agree to first order are separated only at second order, which reduction modulo \((U^2)\) discards. That is the defect's mechanism exactly. It suggests the fix: look at second-order data, meaning witnesses that see \((U^2)\) modulo \(s'^2\), where the row-sum ideal on the board with column 1 would have to be refined. Test. Passed: the observed rank modulo \(R\) is exactly the first-order bound \(1+2m=7\), and the rank in \(G\) exceeds it through second-order terms.

trail.text: Degenerate perturbation theory. Its advice was to look at second-order data. In the column representation the tops are exactly first order in \(\tilde A\) (lem:column-representation (3)), and the \(U\)-shifted defect was a representation artifact. Follow-up. Closed: the second-order data it pointed to vanish in the right representation.

text: Jordan type and the Lefschetz properties (Harima, Maeno, Morita, Numata, Wachi, Watanabe, The Lefschetz Properties , LNM 2080, 2013; Iarrobino, Macias Marques, McDaniel, Artinian algebras and Jordan type , 2022). Target: obstacle (a). Answers. Freeness of \(\operatorname{gr}F^Q\) over \(\mathbb F_3[u]/(u^3)\) says that multiplication by \(u\) has Jordan type \((3,\dots,3)\), that is, \(u\) and \(u^2\) have maximal rank in the filtered sense. Maximal rank is the property that Lefschetz theory proves for algebras far from any pullback, by degeneration to monomial or torus-fixed algebras and by Hilbert-function arguments. It is a route to row freeness that does not need joint freeness. Test. Passed: prop:spread-family-level-gap is a Jordan-type statement. Its level gap \(H_{Q_0}(d)>H_{Q_1}(d)\) forces a Jordan block of \(r_i\) shorter than 3 in degree about \(e\). The criterion of prop:single-direction-sectors is equality of the level-set Hilbert functions, which is Jordan type \((3^c)\) through \(D-2\). This check shows the translation is consistent with the proved results. It is no evidence yet that Lefschetz methods reach families beyond capacity.

trail.text: Jordan type. The Jordan-type lead entry reduced it to recorded statements. Follow-up. Closed: no mechanism beyond those statements.

text: The Alexander–Hirschowitz theorem and the Horace method (Alexander and Hirschowitz, 1995; Brambilla and Ottaviani's short proof, 2008). Target: obstacle (a) for generic families. Answers. Clause tops are products of squares, that is, double points. AH says generic double points impose independent conditions outside a finite list of exceptions, and the Horace method proves it by specializing points onto a hyperplane and inducting. Row freeness beyond capacity for generic members is a relative version, independence modulo the row sums, and a Horace induction that specializes members onto one column is the matching tool. Test. Passed: the row Horace and glued double points entries run exactly this induction for selectors at degrees 3 and 4. Random product tops behave like random matrices up to the fill point ( generic directness ). What is missing is the relative, modulo-row-sums version at degree \(\Theta(\log n)\).

trail.text: Alexander–Hirschowitz and the Horace method. The same entry showed that a Horace step is hole splitting with the fiber-lattice terms. Follow-up. Closed: reduced to conj:fiber-lattice-freeness.

text: Gauge fixing and the Gribov ambiguity (theoretical physics; Gribov 1978, Singer 1978). Translation: representing a family modulo the row equations is choosing a gauge. Normal form is an axial gauge, the column representation another gauge, and the PHP-level ideal is the gauge-invariant content. Singer's theorem says a global gauge slice can fail to exist for topological reasons, while local gauges always exist. Answers. Obstacle (b) looks like a Gribov obstruction. On the patch where row \(i\) holds at most one pigeon, the functional localization works, and the partial-row family is a local gauge. The failure sits on the multi-pigeon patch. The remedy the bridge suggests is to fix the gauge patchwise and glue the patches by Mayer–Vietoris, rather than to seek one global equivalent family. Test. Passed: on the functional patch, \(x_{ic}r_i^{(1)}=x_{ic}\), so the varying-shift spread family has its pullback equivalent there, as computed above. The gluing across patches is open.

trail.text: Gauge fixing. Developed into empty-row sculpting, whose value-fiber conjecture is refuted. Fall closure, the other natural gauge, reverses the level gap, as shown above. Follow-up. Closed: every gauge built from the members fails on non-distributive confinements, and gauges that add points are not constructible by the tools at hand.

text: Linkage and the Mayer–Vietoris sequence of ideals (Peskine and Szpiro, Liaison des variétés algébriques , Invent. Math. 26, 1974). Target: the gluing of confined pieces. Answers. The sequence \(0\to R/(I\cap J)\to R/I\oplus R/J\to R/(I+J)\to0\) and its linkage refinements compute the invariants of a union from the pieces and a connecting map. A lift that is row-free must make that connecting map vanish, so the choice of lift becomes the choice of how the pieces glue. Test. Passed: the class \(r_i\tau\) of prop:confinement-nondistributivity is that connecting term. \(\tau\) lies in both pieces' top ideals and not in the union's.

trail.text: Linkage and the Mayer–Vietoris sequence of ideals. It identified \(r_i\tau\) as a connecting term. Follow-up. Closed: after the subset reframing, structured families need no gluing of their pieces, since one pullback piece suffices.

text: Restrictions that pin rows (Beame and Pitassi, Simplified and improved resolution lower bounds , FOCS 1996; Razborov's restriction method for PHP). Target: row-local families. Answers. A restriction assigning row \(i\)'s pigeon removes its row-local perturbations. Each member becomes the core plus a constant, so the family becomes a sunflower with constants inside joint capacity. It is treated by restriction rather than by equivalence. Test. Passed for one row: pinning row \(i\) to a column \(c\) turns the varying-shift family into \(\{L,L+a_ce_0\}\), a two-member core. It breaks when many rows carry perturbations, where the record's per-pigeon rank cap applies ( row-local review ).

trail.text: Restrictions that pin rows. A confined base is the subset analogue of pinning one row, and it is what the reframing uses. Follow-up. Closed: absorbed into lem:row-free-subset-sufficiency's pieces.

text: Zeon algebras and nilpotent adjacency matrices (Schott and Staples, Nilpotent adjacency matrices, random graphs and quantum random variables , J. Phys. A 41, 155205, 2008). Translation: commuting generators with \(\zeta^2=0\) are the cell variables of \(G\) before the row sums. A square \(\ell^2=2\sum_{u<v}a_ua_vx_ux_v\) is a weighted edge sum on the cells. So \(\Pi_b\) is a generating function of weighted matchings of \(2t\) edges, two drawn from each prefix quadric, and the collision relations delete every matching that covers two cells of one column. Then \(\chi(s\Pi_b)\) is a matching sum. Answers. Zeon calculus computes moments of such matching sums in closed form. Mod 3, that could give the distribution of \(\chi(s\Pi_b)\) for monomial and other structured \(\chi\), where the Gauss bound is weakest. Test. Passed: the identity \((\sum a_ux_u)^2=2\sum_{u<v}a_ua_vx_ux_v\) and the product expansion are exact in \(\mathbb F_3[x]/(x_u^2)\), and the collisions delete exactly the matchings covering two cells of a column. Whether the closed forms survive reduction mod 3 and the row sums is the open step.

trail.text: The zeon translation passed in the moment review. Work this cycle: for a squarefree monomial \(x_S\) with at most one cell per column, and forms \(\ell_i=\sum_ua_{iu}x_u\), put \(A_j=\sum_ic_{ji}a_ia_i^{\mathsf T}\). Work in the collision algebra \(\mathbb F_3[x]/(x_u^2,\ x_ux_v\text{ for }u,v\text{ in one column})\), before the occupancy relation and the row sums, where these monomials form a basis. Then the coefficient of \(x_S\) in \(\ell_k^2\Pi_b\) is, up to sign, the coefficient of \(z_0z_1^2\cdots z_t^2\) in the hafnian of the pencil \(z_0a_ka_k^{\mathsf T}+\sum_jz_jA_j\) restricted to \(S\). The constant is \(2^{3t+1}\), a unit mod 3. Each of the \(2t+1\) edge-sum factors carries a 2, and the ordered pair of copies of each \(\sigma_j\) contributes \(2^t\). The collision relations delete nothing inside such an \(S\). Every functional of lem:block-conditioned-moment pulls back to a combination of these monomial coefficients. So its kill probabilities are distributions mod 3 of combinations of pencil-hafnian coefficients as the prefix varies. Follow-up. Closed: zeon calculus evaluates sums over all labels, such as traces of powers of nilpotent adjacency matrices, and says nothing about the distribution of one fixed coefficient mod 3. No equidistribution theory for hafnian coefficients mod 3 is known.

text: The basis of Impagliazzo, Pudlák and Sgall (ECCC TR97-042, Definition 2.5 and Proposition 2.8). Target: the PC lift. Answers. The basis \(B_d\) makes the PC closure of the pigeon axioms explicit, as \(\operatorname{span}(B_d\setminus T_d)\), with the monotonicity \(x_aQ_i\in B_d\) iff \(x_a\in B_{d-1}\) and \(i\notin\mathrm{dom}(a)\). PC hardness with clauses becomes 1 outside the \(R(x_{ij}\cdot)\)-closure of the \(R(C)\). The dance line's zero-prescribed designs are the first step of that closure. Test. Passed as a translation, checked against Definition 2.5, Proposition 2.8 and Theorem 2.9 of the source. The caveat is that the source's identities include the functional axioms \(x_{ij}x_{ij'}=0\), which the weak base lacks.

trail.text: The Impagliazzo–Pudlák–Sgall basis. Work this cycle: none needed. The design lift criterion poses the lift on functions on the allowed set of weak PHP, with no basis and no functional axioms. Follow-up. Closed: superseded by prop:design-lift-criterion.

text: Cone constructions for coboundary expansion (Gromov, 2010; Kozlov and Meshulam, Quantitative aspects of acyclicity , 2019). Target: multi-face coboundaries. Answers. A symmetric complex with a cone structure has every nonzero coboundary supported on many faces. For chessboard complexes this would make a sparse excluded set unlikely to contain one. Test. Passed in the model with independent exclusions. The smallest coboundary support, a single face's coface set, has \(N-k+1\) matchings. There are at most \(n^{2k}\) faces, and each coface set lies wholly in an excluded set of density \(O(1/n)\) with probability \(O(1/n)^{N-k+1}\) under independence. The union bound \(n^{2k}O(1/n)^{N-k+1}\) is \(o(1)\) in the relevant regime \(k\le D=O(\log n)\ll N\). The correlated exclusions of W_RS are outside that model.

trail.text: Cone constructions for coboundary expansion. Work this cycle: prop:top-drop-coordinates identified the relevant cochains at the top level, unsigned pigeon cochains on \((D-1)\)-matchings. Their coboundary may equal superset patterns of excluded smaller matchings instead of vanishing. Expansion would bound the pairs without superset terms, but the carrier \(\mathcal Q_D\) is excluded, and the cochains on \(\mathcal A\) are not yet written. Follow-up. Continuing.

Cone constructions for coboundary expansion. Work this cycle: the lead was checked against the current form of the obstacle. The top obstruction cochains of prop:top-drop-coordinates live on the truncated carrier, which the lift review excluded. On the full allowed set the obstruction is the splitting condition (S), which is not a question about cochain supports. Follow-up. Closed: the cochain formulation belongs to an excluded carrier.

text: Warning propagation and the cavity method (Mézard, Parisi and Zecchina, Science 297, 2002). Translation: a face exclusion is a warning sent to the parent face, and a cascade is warning propagation up the recursion. The set of faces with forced zeros is the core. Answers. The cavity method's threshold for a core decides whether forced zeros percolate. Test. Passed in the model with independent exclusions. A warning reaches a parent only if all of about \(n\) extensions of it by one pigeon are forced. Given the warning at hand, the other \(n-1\) extensions must also be forced. Each warning has about \(n\) parent-and-pigeon pairs, so at density \(O(1/n)\) the expected number of new warnings per warning is about \(n\cdot O(1/n)^{n-1}\ll1\), which is subcritical. Correlation through shared value vectors is outside the model.

trail.text: Warning propagation. Work this cycle: under PC on \(\mathcal Q_D\), a forced zero at an excluded \(U\) spreads to every superset within degree \(D\) (truncation forcing), not only to the parent faces. The subcritical estimate of the dance review holds for the Nullstellensatz recursion, but the PC process is supercritical, as the bootstrap bridge computes. Follow-up. Closed: the question moves to the threshold on \(\mathcal A\), carried by the bootstrap bridge.

text: Bootstrap percolation (Aizenman and Lebowitz, Metastability effects in bootstrap percolation, J. Phys. A 21, 1988). Translation: PC's multiplication of a derived multiple \(x_U\) to all supersets is a monotone infection of the matching lattice from the excluded matchings. On \(\mathcal Q_D\) the threshold is one infected submatching. On \(\mathcal A\), infection needs a drop, which is a higher threshold. Answers. Bootstrap theory locates the critical density at which infection spreads, which would say whether a support survives PC's forcing. Test. Passed as a translation on \(\mathcal Q_D\). With threshold one, the surviving fraction of \(D\)-matchings is about \(e^{-2^D\delta}\) in the independence model, so the process is supercritical, matching truncation forcing. The threshold on \(\mathcal A\) is not identified.

trail.text: Bootstrap percolation. Work this cycle: on \(\mathcal A=P\setminus E\), PC's forcing needs a drop. A drop comes from a function of low degree supported on \(E\) whose top lies in the row-sum ideal without splitting. So the infection threshold on \(\mathcal A\) is the sparsity at which \(E\) begins to support such functions, a question about low-degree functions on sparse sets. Follow-up. Continuing.

Bootstrap percolation. Work this cycle: truncated inclusion–exclusion gives the infection a concrete threshold. A reweighted design errs only on points infected by at least \(k+1\) blocks. The threshold question becomes whether those errors can be absorbed. Follow-up. Continuing, now as the Bonferroni lead.

Bootstrap percolation. Work: the infection threshold is now explicit. PHP's forcing reaches every deep-overlap point through the products \(1_{E_b}W_a\), so infection is supercritical whenever deep overlaps exist. Follow-up. Closed: the threshold is emptiness.

text: Replica symmetry in random constraint satisfaction (Achlioptas and Coja-Oghlan, Algorithmic barriers from phase transitions, FOCS 2008). Translation: the allowed set is the solution space of a random CSP with one constraint per block, and top-lift subsets are clusters. Answers. Below the clustering threshold the solution space is one well-connected piece. Its typical subsets inherit the whole space's properties, which would make \(\mathcal A\) itself a top-lift subset. Test. Passed as a translation. The excluded density is \(O(1/n)\), so \(\mathcal A\) is all but a vanishing fraction of \(P\), deep in the replica-symmetric regime. This gave the reformulation above: \(I(\mathcal A)\) consists of the functions supported on the sparse set \(E\). It does not by itself give (S).

trail.text: Replica symmetry. Work this cycle: the Bonferroni lead uses the replica-symmetric picture directly. At a fixed point the blocks' exclusions are independent, each with probability at most \(3^{-t}\), so \(r\) is nearly Poisson with mean at most \(M3^{-t}\). Points with \(r>k\) are then rare, with probability at most \(\binom M{k+1}3^{-t(k+1)}\) at each point. Follow-up. Developed into the Bonferroni lead.
Replica symmetry. Work: its sparse-set picture drove the Bonferroni and Lucas constructions, which closed on hiding. Follow-up. Closed with them.

text: Truncated inclusion–exclusion (Bonferroni, Teoria statistica delle classi e calcolo delle probabilità, 1936). Target: the Nullstellensatz half at the dense core, at a cost independent of \(M\). Let \(h_k=\sum_{j\le k}(-1)^je_j(1_{E_1},\dots,1_{E_M})\), with \(e_j\) the elementary symmetric polynomials in the blocks' excluded indicators. At a point lying in exactly \(r\) excluded sets, \(h_k=1\) if \(r=0\), \(h_k=0\) if \(1\le r\le k\), and \(h_k=(-1)^k\binom{r-1}k\) if \(r>k\). With separators of degree at most \(s\le2h+4t\), \(h_k\) has degree at most \(ks\), whatever \(M\) is. Answers. Let \(\lambda_0\) be any PHP design of degree \(D\le\lceil N/2\rceil\), which exists over every field (see the correction below). Put \(\lambda_k(f)=\lambda_0(fh_k)\). Then \(\lambda_k\) vanishes on the row multiples \(x_S\rho_i\) with \(|S|\le D-ks-1\), because \(\lambda_0\) kills all row multiples up to degree \(D\). On a clause multiple, \(\lambda_k(x_SC_b)=\lambda_0(x_SC_bh_k)\), and \(C_bh_k\) is supported on the points lying in at least \(k+1\) excluded sets. Here a clause \(C_b=g_i\,[Cg=0]\) is nonzero only where \(g_i=1\) and \(Cg=0\), hence only on \(E_b=\{g\ne0,\ Cg=0\}\), where \(r\ge1\). So the per-block cost of separators becomes a cost per overlap depth. In the terms of lem:multiplier-designs, \(h_k\) is an approximate multiplier. An exact multiplier must vanish on all of \(E\), and product multipliers stop at about \((N-D)/2\) blocks. \(h_k\) vanishes on \(E\) except on the \((k+1)\)-fold overlaps, in degree \(ks\). That lemma's open vanishing-degree question becomes a question about those overlaps. Test. Passed as a translation: the design property and the support of the errors are the computations above. Not shown: that \(\lambda_k(1)\ne0\), and that the overlap errors vanish or can be corrected. \(\lambda_0\) is not a measure on dense functions, so small support does not make the errors small.

trail.text: Truncated inclusion–exclusion. Work: developed into lem:lucas-truncation and prop:lucas-multiplier-reduction; prop:hiding-needs-emptiness showed that its hiding condition needs empty deep overlaps. Follow-up. Closed: emptiness is out of the design range for dense families.

text: Semi-regular sequences and the degree of regularity (Bardet, Faugère and Salvy, On the complexity of Gröbner basis computation of semi-regular overdetermined algebraic equations, ICPSS 2004). Target: the room in the problem. Answers. If PHP plus the clauses behaved like a semi-regular system, its first fall would come at the first nonpositive coefficient of the Hilbert series, far above \(D\). Test. Passed as a translation: the arithmetic above gives about \(n^2\). This is the record's A3 heuristic in the language of the source, so it restates rather than resolves the adversarial case.

trail.text: Semi-regular sequences. Work: compared with this review's falsification attempt. The semi-regular heuristic predicts room, and random prefixes defeat covering attacks, but neither gives a certificate for adversarial forms. Follow-up. Closed: it restates open statement A3 and supplies no mechanism for A1.

text: Shannon's rate–distortion trade-off (A mathematical theory of communication, 1948). Translation: a certificate must encode which points are excluded. A clause spends degree \(4t+2\) to carry \(t\log_23\) bits of exclusion, about \(0.4\) bits per degree. A cell variable carries about \(\log_2n\) bits per degree. Answers. A rate bound would turn the exchange-rate barrier into a lower bound for pointwise multipliers: degree at least the information in \(E\) divided by the best rate. Test. Passed as a translation: the arithmetic shows the clauses are far less efficient carriers than cell monomials, consistent with the barrier. No theorem transfers, since polynomial degree over \(\mathbb F_3\) is not an information measure.

trail.text: Rate–distortion trade-off. Work: the colon multipliers entry showed that base-design certificates are pointwise on the PHP-hard part of \(E\), so a rate bound would only turn the exchange-rate barrier for them into a theorem. Follow-up. Closed: a sharper barrier for a closed programme is off the critical path.

text: Quantum logic (Birkhoff and von Neumann, The logic of quantum mechanics, Ann. of Math. 37, 1936). Translation: in quantum logic, closed subspaces generate a distributive (Boolean) sublattice exactly when their projections commute. Here, a common adapted basis for the members' top ideals is the same as a family of commuting idempotent operators on \(G_D\) with those images: coordinate projections in the basis give such operators, and commuting idempotents are simultaneously diagonalizable. Answers. It turns the search for an adapted basis into a search for commuting idempotents. Multiplication by the indicators \(1_{E_b}\) is a natural candidate. Test. Passed as a translation. In the unfiltered algebra \(F^P\), the ideals \(I(Q_b)=1_{E_b}F^P\) are the images of the commuting idempotents \(f\mapsto1_{E_b}f\), so they generate a Boolean lattice, the lattice of supports. Distributivity can therefore fail only through the degree filtration, in passing to top degree \(D\). The row ideal is all of \(F^P\) there, so its part of the question is also purely a filtration effect.

trail.text: Quantum logic. Work: batched splitting identified the filtration failure it located as a fall, a first syzygy over the row sums of the sum of the members' tops. Follow-up. Closed: the commuting idempotents \(1_{E_b}\) do not respect the degree filtration, and the failure they leave is the open statement itself.

text: Qutrit stabilizer codes (Gottesman, Fault-tolerant quantum computation with higher-dimensional systems, 1998), from quantum information. Translation: through \(g_i=1+r_i\), the row sums generate an elementary abelian 3-group acting on functions on \(Y\) of degree at most \(D\), like a group of qutrit Pauli \(X\)-type operators. Row freeness says that this function space is a sum of regular representations, a code with no nontrivial "logical" fixed subspace for any shifted subgroup. Answers. Code-distance arguments show that no low-weight operator acts trivially on a code space. An analogue would bound the degree at which any shifted direction \(1+\sum\alpha_ir_i\) can fail freeness on \(Y\). Test. Passed as a translation: the group-algebra identification holds in \(G\), since \(r_i^3=0\). No distance-type theorem is identified yet, and the truncated Dade counterexample shows that single-direction control alone does not suffice.

trail.text: Qutrit stabilizer codes. Work: developed in excluded-loss balance into the Frobenius splitting and the necessary level balance, recorded for uniform prefixes as conj:uniform-level-balance. Follow-up. Closed: its content is a necessary condition, and sufficiency needs a special-position form of Dade's lemma that the truncated counterexample rules out in general.

text: Link and star sequences of Stanley–Reisner theory (Hochster's formula; Bruns and Herzog, Cohen–Macaulay Rings, section 5.3). Target: the obstacle. Answers. Multiplying by a shared cell \(y_z\) passes to the link of \(z\), where every clause through \(z\) loses \(z\) and pairwise intersections through \(z\) drop by one. An induction on the shared cells present in a syzygy would reduce \(\lambda\)-intersecting families to \(\lambda-1\), and finally to the direct case. Test. Passed on two clauses sharing two cells at degree \(2h-2\): the part through \(z_1\) reduces in the link to clauses sharing one cell below their direct bound, and \(y_{z_1}\) times their Taylor kernel is Frobenius, as computed above.

trail.text: The link and star sequences lead was developed into thm:shared-cell-induction and thm:pair-reduction, the induction on shared cells through links it proposed. thm:bounded-clusters then made the link induction unnecessary. Follow-up. Closed: developed into two working proofs and superseded by the component count.

text: Rödl's nibble for near-optimal packings (Rödl, On a packing and covering problem, European J. Combin. 6, 1985). Target: the count at a given \(\lambda\). Answers. Packings of \(|U|\)-sets in the \(\approx n^2\) cells with pairwise intersections at most \(\lambda\) reach about \((n^2/|U|)^{\lambda+1}\) sets, against \(n^{\lambda+1}\) for polynomial graphs. So \(n^K\) clauses would need only \(\lambda\approx K/2\), raising the certified degree to about \(2k+4-K/2\). Test. Passed as a count, from the packing bound and the nibble. The column-distinct condition on each support is compatible with it, but the construction is not explicit.

trail.text: Rödl's nibble was to raise the count at fixed \(\lambda\). Under thm:bounded-clusters, \(\lambda\) may grow up to \(h/(2T)\), a constant fraction of \(k\), and the column design with polynomials of degree at most \(\mu=\lambda\) gives about \((n/u)^{\lambda+1}\) explicit clauses, every polynomial count, without packings (the parts grow by \((T-1)\mu\)). Follow-up. Closed: the count is no longer a constraint.

text: Sudoku-style exact covers and Knuth's dancing links (computer science; Knuth, Dancing links, 2000). Translation: the content argument chooses, for a monomial \(R\), a pattern \(Q\) avoiding blocked and shared cells, an exact-cover-like selection. Answers. Counting the valid choices by a covering argument would give explicit size conditions for every level of the link induction. Test. Passed as a translation: the counts used so far (blocked cells at most the degree, shared cells at most \(\lambda\)) are the one-step version, and for \(\lambda\) levels they add, needing \(|S|\ge e+2\lambda+2\) and \(|T_j|\ge e+2\lambda+1\) in the worst case. Column Wilson's \(2e+2\) and \(2e+1\) already exceed these when \(e\ge2\lambda\).

trail.text: The exact-cover counting of pattern choices was to give size conditions for every level of the link induction. The component count of thm:bounded-clusters, a second-order Bonferroni bound on one monomial, replaced it. Follow-up. Closed: the counting it proposed is subsumed by the component count.

text: Percolation: sharpness of the phase transition (Menshikov, Coincidence of critical points in percolation problems, Soviet Math. Dokl. 33, 1986; Aizenman and Barsky, Comm. Math. Phys. 108, 1987). Translation: the exploration of step 2 is a percolation cluster on clauses, whose offspring are the clauses with \(h-j\lambda\) pattern cells in the explored monomial. Answers. Designed families are subcritical, with clusters of at most \(4s/h\) clauses. The dense core is supercritical. Supercritical percolation is handled by coarse-graining (Grimmett and Marstrand), which would group blocks into super-blocks whose syzygies are proved together and whose mutual overlaps are subcritical. Test. Passed as a translation, resting on the heuristic of the section on the mechanism against A1: for dense forms every monomial of degree \(s\) with cells in the right columns meets the patterns of essentially all clauses, the supercritical case, while for designed families the offspring count is at most \(T\). Whether a coarse-graining exists for adversarial families is open.

trail.text: The percolation bridge was developed in the coarse-graining barrier , which proved that support-level coarse-graining leaves a \(\delta^2\) fraction of a dense family in one group. Its coefficient-level successor is conj:pseudorandom-taylor, tracked on its own. Follow-up. Closed: the support form is barred by prop:coarse-graining-barrier.

text: Subspace-evasive sets (Dvir and Lovett, Subspace evasive sets, STOC 2012). Target: the survival condition, which asks whether the added cells' coefficient vectors all lie in one proper subspace \(K_0(z)\). Answers. A deterministic set of vectors meeting every subspace in a family of proper subspaces kills every class; for fixed families this is the derandomization of defect decay. Test. Passed, and reduces to linear algebra: a set of vectors lies in no proper subspace exactly when it spans, so the condition is that the relevant forms are independent off the base, the condition found above. It adds no tool for classes on many tops, where spanning fails by dimension.

trail.text: Subspace-evasive sets reduced, in the dense split review, to spanning of the added cells' coefficient vectors, which prop:relation-avoidance now states exactly: survivors lie in \(\Phi^{-1}(\operatorname{Rel}\otimes V)\). Follow-up. Closed: absorbed into prop:relation-avoidance, with no further tool for classes on many tops.

text: Stopping sets of LDPC codes under erasure decoding (Di, Proietti, Telatar, Richardson and Urbanke, IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory 48, 2002). Translation: non-Taylor classes as erased symbols, columns as checks that remove a class when their coefficients leave its kernel, defect decay as peeling. Answers. Peeling fails exactly on stopping sets; here a class survives only when the forms of its tops have a combination vanishing on all added cells, the analogue of a stopping set, and code design avoids small stopping sets through expansion. For W, the analogue would be a lower bound on how many tops a surviving class must involve. Test. Passed as a translation, by the falsification attempt above: survival forces a vanishing combination.

trail.text: The stopping-set bridge was developed in stopping-set survival : survivors' supports must be stopping sets, of about \(n^2/(K\log_3n)\) tops for random families. Follow-up. Closed: developed into prop:stopping-set-survival; the open part, bounding the supports of base classes, is the route's obstacle above.

text: Soundness of the sum-check protocol (Lund, Fortnow, Karloff and Nisan, J. ACM 39, 1992). Translation: each random column is a challenge that exposes a non-Taylor class with probability at least \(2/3\), as a random evaluation exposes a false polynomial identity. Answers. Derandomized sum-check uses structured challenge sets; for W, the fixed columns are the challenges, and the question is whether they are rich enough. Test. Passed as a translation: cor:defect-decay's bound is this soundness bound, and the deterministic version is the spanning condition.

trail.text: The sum-check bridge's soundness bound is cor:defect-decay's factor 3 per cell, and its derandomization is the spanning condition, both now inside prop:relation-avoidance; this review found the factor-3 count too weak to decide anything by itself. Follow-up. Closed: its content is the relation-avoidance bound.

text: Fröberg's conjecture on generic forms (R. Fröberg, An inequality for Hilbert series of graded algebras, Math. Scand. 56, 1985), with its exterior-algebra analogue (Moreno-Socías and Snellman, Some conjectures about the Hilbert series of generic ideals in the exterior algebra, Homology Homotopy Appl. 4, 2002). Target: the random case. Answers. Generic ideals have the expected Hilbert series for any number of generators, which in the monomial algebra is Taylor generation below the fill point; it is the random case of the obstacle. Test. Passed as a translation: the record already states it for this algebra as conj:maximal-generic-freeness and conj:semi-regular-relative-to-base, both open, so it is a reformulation, not a tool.

trail.text: Fröberg's conjecture as the random case: conj:split-obstructions is now its local form, two base-local properties of random dense tops below half the fill point, with exact data at one size. Follow-up. Continuing: it names what a Fröberg-type statement must give, but is no nearer a proof.
Fröberg's conjecture as the random case: unchanged since the split-line review; conj:split-obstructions remains its local form. Follow-up. Continuing.

Fröberg's conjecture as the random case: developed in single-top Wilson threshold for one generator, where the expected annihilator is proved for every choice of forms; for several generators the free-part criterion covers bounded families. Follow-up. Continuing: the many-generator case is the obstacle above.

Fröberg's conjecture as the random case. Developed in group freeness and base-union socle : freeness over a small family's forms is the expected Hilbert function of their ideal in this truncated setting, and it is now proved on one row, for every choice of forms whose combinations are long, at a factor \(O(F\log F)\) above the necessary length. Follow-up. Closed: its target for single tops and pairs is proved; the many-generator case is the obstacle, where by prop:batched-splitting expected Hilbert functions of the sum are the same Tor-vanishing statement.

text: Compressed sensing and the restricted isometry property (Candès and Tao, Decoding by linear programming, IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory 51, 2005). Translation: \(\operatorname{Rel}\) is the null space of the forms' coefficient matrix off the base; survival needs obstruction coefficients \(\rho_k\) in that null space; the stopping-set bound says null vectors are not sparse. Answers. Restricted isometry makes every sparse vector far from the null space; for W it would say that coefficient vectors \(\rho_k\) supported on few tops are far from \(\operatorname{Rel}\), the stopping-set statement with a margin. Test. Passed as a translation: prop:stopping-set-survival's union bound is the finite-field form of the null space property for random matrices.

trail.text: The compressed-sensing bridge asked for a null-space property of \(\operatorname{Rel}\) against sparse coefficient vectors. Under a split, the vectors to avoid are the directions \(\mu_i\), of weight at most 2 in the data, so the needed null-space property is the column-weight condition at \(t=2\). Follow-up. Closed: absorbed into prop:split-obstruction-bound; the open part is the split itself.

text: Macaulay's inverse systems and colon ideals (F. S. Macaulay, The Algebraic Theory of Modular Systems, 1916; Iarrobino and Kanev, Power Sums, Gorenstein Algebras, and Determinantal Loci, LNM 1721, 1999). Target: the split's pieces. Answers. Colon quotients \((I:\mathfrak m_S)/I\) are dual to the part of the inverse system killed by the cells of \(S\); if each piece \(\mu\otimes W\) is forced into such a colon for \(S\) the support of its combination \(\ell_\mu=\sum_f\mu_fL_f\), dense directions have small pieces. Test. Passed: the cell derivations \(\delta_i=y_i\partial/\partial y_i\) (on several rows \(x_{ic}\partial/\partial x_{ic}\)) preserve the monomial relations, and applying \(\delta_i\) to \(\sum_bz_b\tau_b=0\) gives \(\sum_b\delta_i(z_b)\tau_b+y_i\sum_{b,j}l_{b,j,i}\Phi_{b,j}(z)=0\), so \(y_i\cdot\mathrm{ob}_{l_i}(x)\in I_R\) for every cell \(i\) of \(R\), where \(\mathrm{ob}_{l_i}\) is the obstruction of a new cell with the coefficients of cell \(i\). For a piece \(\mu\otimes w\) this gives \((\mu\cdot l_i)\,y_iw\in I_R\), so \(W_\mu\subseteq\bigcap_{i\in\operatorname{supp}\ell_\mu}(I_R:y_i)/I_R\).

trail.text: The inverse-system lead was developed in colon pieces : pieces lie in relative socles, but the colon counts cells and cannot show that directions have low weight. Follow-up. Closed: it cannot separate directions by weight, and a vanishing colon on small bases is contradicted by the data.

text: Quantum stabilizer codes and the Knill–Laflamme conditions (Knill and Laflamme, Theory of quantum error-correcting codes, Phys. Rev. A 55, 1997). Translation: forms are error operators, \(\operatorname{Rel}\) is the group of undetectable errors, pieces \(\mu\) are logical operators, and the column weight is the code distance. Answers. Knill–Laflamme says errors below the distance are correctable exactly when they act trivially on the code space; in the translation, a survivor is a logical operator, and the split says logical operators have weight at most 2, so a distance above 2 leaves no survivors outside \(W_0/T\). Test. Passed as a translation: prop:split-obstruction-bound is exactly this statement; it adds no mechanism for the split itself.

trail.text: The stabilizer-code translation restated prop:split-obstruction-bound; no cycle found a code-theoretic mechanism for the split itself. Follow-up. Closed: the translation adds no mechanism beyond the proposition.

text: Flat base change for Tor (C. A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Cambridge University Press 1994, Section 3.2: if \(A\) is flat over \(B\), then \(\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(A\otimes_BM,N)\cong\operatorname{Tor}^B_i(M,N)\)). Apply it with \(B=T_i\), the truncated algebra of the \(i\)-th top's own forms, over which \(\widetilde A\) is free through the relevant degree when those forms have long combinations (thm:base-packing-freeness and the transversal argument above). Then \(\widetilde A/\tau_i\widetilde A=\widetilde A\otimes_{T_i}T_i/(\tau_i)\), and \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^{\widetilde A}(\widetilde A/\tau_i\widetilde A,\widetilde A/J_{<i})\), which measures \(\tau_i\widetilde A\cap J_{<i}\) modulo \(\tau_iJ_{<i}\), becomes \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^{T_i}(T_i/(\tau_i),\widetilde A/J_{<i})\). That vanishes when \(\widetilde A/J_{<i}\) is free over \(T_i\). If \(\tau_i\widetilde A\cap J_{<i}=\tau_iJ_{<i}\), a relation \(g\tau_i=\sum_jh_j\tau_j\) splits, with \(g\tau_i=\tau_i\sum_jc_j\tau_j\), into a single-top syzygy \((g-\sum_jc_j\tau_j)\tau_i=0\), Koszul pairs \(\tau_i\tau_j\), and a relation among earlier tops, so induction on \(i\) gives Taylor generation (with Koszul syzygies) of the family through \(D\). Answers. The global step becomes sequential relative freeness: each quotient \(\widetilde A/(\tau_1,\dots,\tau_{i-1})\) free over the next top's own \(k+1\) forms through \(D\). This needs no independence among all \(n^K(k+1)\) forms, which is exactly what made freeness over all forms impossible. Test. Passed at pairs, as an argument: when the two tops' forms are jointly independent with long combinations, \(\widetilde A\) is free over their joint algebra \(T_{12}=T_1\otimes T_2\), so \(\widetilde A/\tau_1\widetilde A=\widetilde A\otimes_{T_{12}}(T_1/(\tau_1)\otimes T_2)\) is free over \(T_2\), and the pair is Taylor-generated. The degree-by-degree form of base change through \(D\), needed for truncated freeness, and the many-top case are not checked; the latter is a new hypothesis, not implied by recorded results.

trail.text: Flat base change. Developed in column-support freeness (prop:sequential-freeness) and tested in relation-length syzygies . Follow-up. Closed: its hypothesis fails for every single linear relation among three tops (ex:three-top-relation-types), and the prefix rule cannot avoid planted relations, so sequential freeness cannot carry W's global step for dependent forms; the relation-length analysis replaces it.

text: Lower bounds for linear 2-query locally decodable and correctable codes (Z. Dvir and A. Shpilka, Locally decodable codes with two queries and polynomial identity testing for depth 3 circuits, SIAM J. Comput. 36, 2007; O. Goldreich, H. Karloff, L. Schulman and L. Trevisan, Lower bounds for linear locally decodable codes and private information retrieval, Comput. Complexity 15, 2006). A linear code whose coordinates are each recoverable from many disjoint pairs has dimension logarithmic in its length. Answers. If every block's squared forms lie in \(\delta M\) disjoint three-term relations, the forms form a linear 2-query correctable code, so their span has dimension \(O(\log M/\delta)\), and the recorded low-rank reductions (pinned-rank vacuity) take over. Relation-rich planted structures would thus be low rank. Test. Passed as a translation for that regime: the Hadamard configuration (all forms of a subspace) attains logarithmic rank, so the bound is of the right shape. It does not reach structures in which each block lies in \(O(1)\) relations, which the bridges below show exist at high rank.

trail.text: Lower bounds for 2-query locally correctable codes. Follow-up. Continuing: not developed in these cycles. It still bounds relation-dense families to logarithmic rank, and it does not reach the sparse high-rank structures of the obstacle.

Lower bounds for 2-query locally correctable codes. Follow-up. Continuing: not developed in these cycles. Their span \(cm=c\log_3(2X+1)\) is logarithmic in the number \(X\) of members, as the lead's dimension bound predicts. Within W's budget that is still not \(O(c)\); whether the pinned-rank reduction handles rank of order \(c\log n\) was not checked.
